layout_details.content: ## B.4.5 Content Language
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The <content-language> element describes the main language used in the XML file
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO Note: Content of the Element
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For ISO standards documents, the content (in 2016) of this element should always be one of "en", "fr", "ru", "es", or "ar".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO Note: Related <language> Element in legacy documents
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For older ISO-related standards only, the <language> element (that is part of the ISO-specific <doc-ident> element) provides the same language information as the <content-language> element, sometimes in a different form. For monolingual documents, <language> and <contentlanguage> will have the same content. However, in each ISO standards document, while the <content-language> element may repeat, there must be a single <language> element, so for documents written in more than one official language, the <language> element will contain a comma-separated (no whitespace) list of language codes for example: "en,fr,de".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This <language> element and usage for multilingual documents has been replaced by a custom metadata item indicating the relevant languages.
layout_details.label: text

```html
<custom-meta>

<meta-name>multilang-ident</meta-name>

<meta-value>en/fr/de</meta-value>

</custom-meta>

```

layout_details.label: text
